segments.text: Hello and welcome to The National Debate.
I'm Mathodas Kapalakrishnan.
Delhi is choking, but its leaders seem busy passing the buck.
Toxic air continues to blanket the national capital and several of the big cities of northern India, with AQI levels stuck in the very poor zone.
But as the Delhi government about the pollution crisis, answers are hard to come by.
The BJP has been pointing fingers at Punjab's stubble burning.
Arm of the party has been hitting back, citing farm fires in BJP rule states.
And as the blame game gathers pace, the national capital continues to breathe poison.
The question is simple.
Who will own this crisis and who's choking accountability?
Joining us to debate this, today we have with us in the studio, Tuhin Sira, National Spokesperson of BJP, Raman Malik, Political Analyst.
We have Alka Kapoor, Principal of Modern Public School, Shailmar Bagh.
We also have Padma Shri, Dr. Sanjeev Bagai, Chairman of Neffron Clinic.
Jayadhar Gupta, is Clean Air Activist.
Joining us, Wing Commander Anum Acharya, Spokesperson of Congress Party is with us.
Let's first take a look at what we're talking about in terms of what the national capital has been going through and what can we expect in coming days.
Well, we have seen of course the rather big question about whether there has been, you know, manipulation of
the AQI in the national capital.
This is what happened on Diwali day, the allegations that data suddenly went blank.
The first finding is that no hourly readings were there across 52 monitoring stations.
The second is that there was large-scale blackout on Diwali night.
The third is that only seven of 59 stations reported proper data in the national capital.
Number four, all 59 stations were fully functional at 8 a.m.
on November 8th.
Data blackout from 9 PM on November 8 to 6 AM on November 9 was the finding.
There's also of course the fact that data stopped after pollution levels approached 1000.
This was the reality check and this was of course widely reported on the day after Diwali.
Now what has been the status of Delhi's toxic air?
We're talking about CPCB data, Delhi's AQI on Diwali Day.
This has been the daily AQI on Diwali where of course pollution typically peaks and we've seen that happen day after day.
What about the last week also?
What is the number that we're looking at?
367 on the 5th of November, 382 on the 6th of November, 369 on the 7th, 376 on 8th,
368 on the 9th, 344 on November 10th and there on it has been largely dipping with 313 on November 11th and on November 12th at 350.
This morning though it has gone up drastically and crossed 400 as well in several parts of Delhi.
Now what is the CPCB's clarification to what we've seen in Delhi?
They have said as far as the AQI data blackout is concerned that the values over 1000 are not included in the 24-hour average from earlier itself.
AQI above 500 remains in the severe category.
There's no change there.
Higher index would not change the health warning is what they've stated.
And capping is in line with the international practice as well.
Private platforms draw from different data sources is their clarification.
Some platforms use instantaneous hourly
readings and that's not the official data, whereas the official AQI uses calibrated, quality assured data is what the CPCB says.
Now let me quickly take this question across to Tuyen.
Tuyen, while this clarification has come in from the CPCB, the government has also clarified that there was no blackout as such, that the full data will be submitted.
There are questions.
There are questions about whether this has happened, typically to try and window-dress the data of Diwali Day, because that's the day when we see a lot of pollution in the National Capital.
Good evening, Madhav.
Good evening, everybody.
First of all, I'm glad that you're having a discussion on this very important subject.

Now, unlike the Congress party, unlike the Ahmadi party, which may want to believe that there is no air pollution in their states, I would be honest to admit that AQI and air pollution is a pan-India problem.
And it needs to be addressed.
And it is being addressed on a war footing.
Now, I will just go.
with some data.
In 2016, since you were talking about Delhi, the total number of days where AQI was above 200 was 189, which has been consistently coming down over the years.
It was 114.
So from 189 days in 2016 when HUI was above 200, now it's 90.
Now there are two important causes, if I may broadly put it into category, of air pollution.
One is the pearly burning, the five palm fires in neighboring states, particularly Punjab at this point of time.
Punjab and Haryana seven or eight years ago would have a similar number of farm fires.
Today, in the last 30 days, Punjab has had 2,500 farm fires.
Haryana, less than 100.
So you see the difference in the trajectory in the last eight years.
Of course, the government has done a few specific things, which I need to point out over here.
Now 4,697 crores worth has been released since 2018-19 for crop residue management funding 3.80 lakh machines and 44,621 custom hiring centers mainly in Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
Now the point is if Haryana and Uttar Pradesh can virtually bring pearly burning to an end, why can't Punjab?
At the same time, since you're talking about Delhi, if I specifically talk about Delhi, from April 2018, India leapfrogged from BS4 to BS6 fuel and vehicles.
One of the biggest beneficiaries have been the urban centers, particularly Delhi and Mumbai.
No PUCC, no fuel.
This is a rule which has been brought by the Delhi government from this year.

You know, a few years ago, the Amadni Party used to always say that we have different governments, they're not cooperating in the NCR region, Delhi government is separate, Haryana government is separate, UP government is separate, and therefore they're not on the same page.
It's a very different scenario for close to two years now.
You've had the Delhi government which is BJP ruled, you have the UP and the Haryana governments which are also BJP ruled.
Why can't all these governments sit together and work out a common action plan?

Because the point is, whether it's public transport, whether it's the vehicular pollution, whether it's the dust pollution, whether it's construction, you know, violations of GRAAP, et cetera, are taking place.
And it's high time that all the governments come down together and have a common plan.
No, no, absolutely.
I completely agree with you, and which is the reason why, you know, the amount which I was mentioning was for all of these five states.
to put an end to farm residue burning.
Now, if Haryana and Uttar Pradesh can achieve its targets, why is Punjab lagging behind?
Delhi, UP, Haryana have been bringing down their parameters.
They have been working actively to bring down farm fires.
It is Punjab that is failing the citizens of Delhi.
Respond.
Okay, first of all, every time you cannot blame the farmers.
every time that the AQI is not right in Delhi, you blame the farmers.
Now practically... Numbers speak for themselves.
Are these numbers fake?
Let me complete, let me complete.
The winds are blowing eastern side.
So all the wind, all the stubble, even if it's burning, it's going towards Pakistan, but they have a problem in Delhi.
Now where is the problem?
There is no wind coming from.
I'll tell you.
This is a completely new definition.
Get your geography right.
East is not, west is Pakistan.
Sir, when western disturbances come, the air comes here.
Sir, please, keep your knowledge with you.
Sir, keep your knowledge with you.
First, fix yourself and fix your parameters.
Don't teach me.
Disturb people.
How did they manipulate the AQI data?
I will tell you.
We had 39 AQM monitoring stations at the peak areas where there used to be a lot of pollution.
They have put 20 AQM monitors in JNU, in the ridge area, in the forested green-lined areas where you will not have PM2 worldwide.
So the average out that comes is basically reduced.
So they are manipulating the data.

52 out of the 59 monitors shut down during Diwali night so the AQI next day because it's a cumulative effect of 24 hours the values go down then they should say oh we have reduced so much tell me something what have they spent on pollution in the last one year I'll give you the numbers Delhi government pollution control and emergency budget was 300 crores
spent only 121 crores.
MCD sweeping and fogging budget was 60 crores, spent zero.
DPCC has a budget of 70 crores, spent zero.
They've done nothing.
And I'll give you a very funny example.
From Delhi, we had the EV fleet going towards Anand Vihar.
So we are controlling pollution.
From the UP side, you have a diesel bus coming towards Anand Vihar.
Are you controlling the pollution?
This is how you're going to control.
From Delhi, you set an EV bus.
From the UP side, it's a diesel bus that is coming.
And they have governments in all the states.
Indian Institute of Tropical and Meteorology, which is the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which says less than 7% is the contribution of Parali in the pollution in Delhi.
Now, you know what is the top two cities, top two cities which is the most polluted, top two cities.
It may be 7 percent, it may be higher, I am not getting into that, but I want Raman Malik.
One second, one second, one second.
There are many who have not even made their opening statements, let's not do this.
But Raman Malik, I am going to put some questions that Chirag has put across because these are all staring at us in the face.
Areas where the pollution monitoring centers are being put are in largely green areas.
Those areas see 24x7 sprinkling of water.
Is there a concerted attempt at trying to control the pollution data?
And is this how Delhi's pollution will be controlled?
If you don't address the core of the issue, the root of the problem, how will we address pollution?
Madhav, simple.
Were they built just before Diwali by the BJP government or this government?
No.
They were there and they are not new centers.
Are they new centers?
Are they new centers?
They have been installed by the BJP government.
In our government it was 39.
Let's understand.
Let's move away from the 50 odd something and let's talk about those 39.
They were there when these people were in government.

One, secondly, how does it happen that in the time that Arvind Kejriwal is the Chief Minister, you can have Punjab as a problem, but once he becomes the de facto super CM of Punjab, Punjab is not a problem.
How can that happen?
Third point, which is very important.
Now you are talking about a particular issue of spike on the day of Diwali and then the numbers also prove that the consistency has been there otherwise.
So my point is simple that there was a data which came about 1152 fires on the day of Diwali.
Where did that come from?
One.
Second,
We have been aware of the nefarious activities of Hamadmi party just to prove their point they can do anything.
And they have done multiple times such act.
Now, my point is… So, what is the nefarious activity here?
that there are stories which are there from the journalists in Punjab and multiple journalists have spoken to me on record on my phone.
So I have that.
So they said that it was a very clear, systematic information transfer.
And it was in the flight?
Regarding?
The producer was in the flight.
Regarding pollution.
About Sangrur, specifically Sangrur.
Sangrur and adjoining areas was the epicenter of stubble burning.
If you want to see, travel around this time to Sangrur, on the highway you will see fire burning like anything.
Why?
When it is known for the last three years that Sangrur has been the epicenter, why did Mr. Bhagwant Maan, who between let's say 10 to 6 is an acting Chief Minister,
cannot go and give some grant there for getting the processes on.
What is happening and what is really causing the Parali burning?

15 to 20 days is the gap between harvest and the next sowing is during that time that we see this Parali burning happening, the crop deadline and delays in field preparation risk the next crop as well.
There's also pest concerns, leftover stubble can invite pests and diseases, which is of course one of the issues, high cost of stubble management machinery, which can cost up to one crore rupees.
Can governments not afford it?

Small farmers struggle to afford the expensive equipment, certainly should be coming in from the government, whether in Punjab or in the other states, and that is some of the problems that we see as far as Parali burning is concerned.
What is the issue related to farm fires and what is the data that we're looking at?
The total data.
September 15 to November 12, 2026 Punjab top of the charts and by a mile at 5,571.
This is of a total of 10,805.
So half, 50% of the recorded farm fires are from there.
Madhya Pradesh at 2,506.
We're also talking about Rajasthan at 1,406.

We're also talking about Uttar Pradesh at 886 in terms of the total amount of farm fires, Haryana far lesser at 218, Uttarakhand at 216, Delhi at two in terms of the recorded farm fires across India over this close to two month period.
Punjab Parali fire, which are the five districts that lead the count?
And remember that these cases in specific districts are even more than some of the neighboring states.
Firozpur itself, 728 cases till November 12th.
Tarantaran, at 687 cases till November 12th.
Sangroor, the district that was being referred to, the Chief Minister Bhagwat Man's district, at 628 cases.
We're also talking about Bhatinda at 499 cases and in Patiala at 374 cases till November 12th.
Now Chirag Sethi, I want you to answer this.
How is it that Punjab is so far higher?
You keep talking about we brought it down from 80,000 to 10,000.
But you're still far ahead of the rest.
How can you justify this kind of fire burning?
Madhav, when we formed the government in 2022, the parali numbers were 80,000.
We got it down to 5,000.
How?
We got 1,48,000 machines.
We were renting it out to the farmers, to the organizations, to the panchayat at an 80% subsidy.
They can use that machine at which they're about 2,500.
It's already 5,500.
Have you brought it down?
Because it's already 5,500 and the season's not over yet.
For 80,000, we've gone to 5,000.
Another 2-3 weeks of Paraji burning will happen, it will reach 10,000 easily.
And there are also serious charges that you are doing this in the night to avoid being detected by satellites.
There are several experts who actually put out, in fact I will just quote that to you, the data.
I quote the data that you know you have actually been orchestrating that.
Respond to that charge because a very serious charge that has been, this is Dr. Hiren Jetwa, an aerosol remote sensing scientist.
He says he's associated with NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center.
He estimates there are 34,000 farm fires across Punjab and Haryana between October 1 and November 9.
It's a massive gap in the data.
Okay, like I said, even if we assume that 1100 fires happened, how did the smoke reach Delhi in one hour?
The wind speed, which is taught in seventh class, which I don't expect people to know, that it takes at least 70 hours for the air to reach Delhi.
How can it reach Delhi in one hour?
Let us say it is not reached in three days.
Has it not reached the national capital?
Are we not breathing 400 HQI?
Let me complete at least.
Then there is another organization by the Government of India, SUFFER.
which suggested that the Parali contribution to Diwali pollution is about 5%.
And you can fact check me if I'm wrong, you can fact check me that it's only 5%.
We have gone down from 80,000 to 5,000 but there are states which are adding up.
Did you see Uttarakhand in the last three years?
Why Uttarakhand is burning this?
Did you see Rajasthan?
It's far less than the problem.
You have to look at proportionality.
The other states are going up now.
We are coming down.
We are in the downward trend.
The other states are in the upward trends.
Please see.
But they are nowhere close to you.
They are nowhere close to the 5,000 odd fires which have already happened from September 15th to November 12th.
We started from 18,000.
In four years, we reduced it to 95%.
It is coming from Punjab down to the plains.
It is not going from the plains up to Punjab.
So he has Pakistan in the east and the winds going to the west.

In 2019, if Kejriwal tells school children to write letters to Captain Amrinder Singh about the pollution in Delhi, now should the Delhi children be writing letters to Uncle Kejriwal or Uncle Bhagwan Man?
Madhav, we have already shown the work we have done.
Please tell me which is the other state which is on a decline.
All the numbers from the previous have gone up.
But we are the only state which has gone down from 80,000 to 15,000.
We are the only state which has actually gone down.
Is that factually correct and have they done enough?
Look, I want to drop a truth bomb here because I am politically agnostic.
All the data that you've shared up here, whether it's the data of the AQI data of Delhi or the data of the farm fires, nothing is accurate.
This is one big smog wash.
I have better monitoring equipment than CPCB and I can tell you with confidence our AQI is not in the 300s at all.
So that's also all a big smog wash.

As far as what you're talking about the NASA scientists, what they are talking, what the NASA scientist is referring to, what Punjab is doing very successfully and I'm sure all the states of India are doing it because agri residue burning is a common practice across all poor developing nations.
This is not just a Punjab problem, it's a pan-India problem.
And central and state governments need to engage with it.
I don't want to stand here and start shooting bullets at anybody in particular here, because it's a pan-India problem.
All the data is managed.
The farmers are told when Punjab is in the blackout phase of the satellite and that's when they burn.
The collectors distribute this information.
So what data are we presenting?
The only data that matters is that I came out here from an ICU because I was gasping for air two days ago and I'm pumped up on steroids.
And my children cannot leave the house.
They can't go to school.
Everybody is gasping for air.
There is a hopelessness.
That's the only data that matters.
And I think these people are shameful and without a conscience if they're just standing here and doing this bickering because this is just such a waste of time.
We need to be doing something positive rather than getting involved in this negative activity.
The point is this, that the future of children is being impacted.
How is, you know, children sitting at home and taking online classes a solution to Delhi's pollution?
Of two to three months of that we see every year and you are of course the principal of a prominent school in Delhi.
What is the solution?
Because this ultimately impacts the health, the lives and our future of India.
So,
First of all, I'm not here as a political analyst.
I'm not looking at pollution from the lens of any politician.
So I'm an educator, and I will give all the perspectives of an educator.
It's causing problems and my children or any other child is not breathing a BJP air or a Congress air or an armed party air.
They are breathing this polluted air which is certainly detrimental to their health and we need immediate action.
But blaming it to the present government, I do not agree.
I certainly do not agree.
I've seen this government closely working.
I've been a part of their few committees and I know what kind of hard work is going on because we've kind of inherited it from the previous governments.
And just in one and a half years time, I think we've done quite a bit.
Certainly, it's not in the interest of the students to sit at home.
Logistics sometimes do not permit.
Hybrid mode of learning is a bad mental and social consequence for them, but they are compelled to stay.
So as a school, we cannot manufacture clean air, but we can certainly manufacture awareness, and that's what we are trying to do.
Let me quickly bring up in fact what has happened in Delhi and this is what is happening in Delhi right now.
Ladies and gentlemen, this is the lung of a Delhi resident currently.
In fact, that's the kind of black inside that doctors get when they open up the lung surgically and this is a healthy lung.
Unfortunately, in some cases, even children happen to have black lungs in Delhi.
And let me bring up the doctor on our panel.
In fact, I'd like you to come in on this Dr. Bagai and tell us what exactly are we looking at?
We are looking at a public health emergency in Delhi.
It's not just about respiratory problems or the coughs or the allergies that we get and infections that we get subsequently, but this is impacting our neurological problems, our cardiac health,
multiple levels that this is actually impacting on citizens in NCR.
How are we going to be a Wixit bar at 2047 if this is the quality of air we are breathing?
So I think some of the people in the neighboring states have taken the song of those seriously, come on baby light my fire.
I think that's on a lighter note.
But more seriously, I think breathing has become a luxury in Delhi.
We can't go out, there is indoor pollution too.
Now, I want all the viewers to understand that when you're talking in terms of the pollution, we are losing approximately 20 lakh Indians every year.
This is 10 times the load of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
That's the depth.
Let it sink in.
This is every year.
That was once in 80, 90, 100 years.
The issue is that all your particulate matter, be it from toxic gases, volatile organic compounds, hydrofluorocarbons, carcinogens, micro-nanoplastics, heavy metal aerosolized,

enter into the body, form very very fine ultra-fine particles, go through the lung barrier, enter your bloodstream, they enter your brain, they involve your cognitive function, there is more than sixty percent decline in memory and cognitive function, there is a twice increase in autism, there is a three hundred percent increase in autism in the last couple of decades, it increases the risk of heart attacks, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, it involves the pregnancies, we are seeing
Twice the number of children being born with congenital abnormalities, stillbirths, premature delivery, spontaneous abortions, mother's health getting affected, maternal diabetes during pregnancy.
There are children who are born with congenital heart disease, absent kidneys, abnormal urinary bladder.
The bone health, the anemias which we are seeing, a lot of it is contributory because of air pollution.
Now we can go on and on about the statistics and how much it increases, but let this also sink in.
A mere 10% increase in PM2.5 gives you a two-fold, that means 200% increase in cardiorespiratory metabolic death.
That's a huge number.
Delhi is carrying the burden because it's landlocked and a lot of geographic disadvantage it has.
The real issue now is we need to get an iron force to manage this pollution.
If India under the present government could manage once in a lifetime catastrophe like COVID, there is no reason to disbelieve that we cannot tackle the air pollution aftermath.
We cannot expect wonders within a month, not even in a year.
But let there be a rollout plan over five years.
But in this particular endeavor, I want the government to involve the scientists, the doctors, the environmentalists.
Yes, there will be a minister.
There will be a bureaucrat.
Let this be scientifically run.
Give clear timelines and deadlines as to what our achievement goals every quarter is.
If other countries can do it, we can do it.
What are the solutions that we see globally as well?
In fact, this is of course the first action that we can possibly do is shutting down of regional coal power plants.
This has been seen in Beijing, in China and whether vehicle registration quotas can be enforced.
In London, in UK, we're looking at city entry fee for polluting vehicles.
The second action is that coal burning ban has been strictly enforced there.
We're also talking about another city that is Mexico, where polluting industry shifted outside the city.
The second action is expanded electric and rapid public transit.
We're also, of course, talking about Tokyo and Japan, where they impose strict particulate filters on diesel.
Early controls on factory emissions were seen here in Japan as well.
In Los Angeles, mandated catalytic converters on all cars and the regional ports shifted to zero emission equipment.
Let me come across to Wing Commander Anum Acharya.
Before we get into the solutions, can any political party today say that they are not responsible for it?
Of course, Congress was not in Delhi for the last, say, 10 to 12 years, but the point is in Punjab not so long ago.
And we all remember the fights that Aravind Kejriwal and Captain Amrinder Singh had on social media in relation to the same issue of Parali burning and pollution from Punjab.
No amount of political debates can legitimize or give a conclusion to this kind of a problem because it affects everyone.
Six days ago I was here.
Today I can hardly speak because I'm suffering from laryngitis.
The pollution has suppressed my vocal cord.
So it is basically a public health issue.
The government of Delhi has been collecting
ECC, that is environmental compensation charges for last 10 years, they have a corpus of about 1,985 crore rupees, 1,985 crore rupees, and they have, till date, they have spent only 781 crore rupees.
So, whatever solutions you have shown for China or Mexico or other countries, they can all be implemented here.
But what we are doing, we are managing, manipulating the appearances.
We are managing the AQI.
Why can't we take this as a problem?
Like Sheila Dixitji, you yourself said, eight, nine years, this problem is persisting.
When Sheila Dixit ji has imposed CNG entirely, the AQI was 93 in 2009.
So, if somebody has already done, it only requires a willingness, it requires a sequence of, you know, pursuance, and then people should come out with solutions.
No arguments like this will do anything for us.

because this is affecting your lungs, my lungs, our blood, that PM2.5 is affecting our blood also, the doctor is already here, I don't have to say but I have done my MPhil in biochemistry, so I'm just saying this kind of effect is happening and the government is responsible, they should spend some money and this is the time
Any government anywhere should take the necessary course correction at the time when it is, and everybody knows it happens more in November, December, January, half of the January.
So why can't at that time we can stop some construction work?
We can just, you know, whatever.
That is there in the graph 4.
That is there in the graph 4.
And sprinkling of water off, not near the IQI centers, to all the countrymen, all the people of the country.
Yeah, but one of the questions that is also there is that Supreme Court has given an order.
And I'm not somebody who says they're completely banned Diwali crackers.
People would have different views.
But there has to be some sense of responsibility.

Because not only was the green cracker rule violated, because there were regular crackers that were, in fact, burst, but also people way beyond the Supreme Court mandated deadline, way into midnight, who are continuing to burst crackers.
So there is a serious issue of actually implementing what the courts have said in the laws of the land as well.
Well, so far as the choice of trackers is concerned, like somebody else has mentioned, principal ma'am had mentioned, it has to be about individual responsibility as well.

You know, the government, in fact, the Maharashtra government had spoken about green trackers, but eventually at the end of the day, banning everything is not something the government should ideally do.
The onus has to be on the individual.
And I'm sure, you know, when you see your kids suffering,
Individuals will take a conscious choice depending upon the situation that exists in a given state.
Tugin, you have banned, your government has banned commercial use of diesel taxis.
Why can't that be done for private cars?
When are we going to take drastic measures?
You have to ultimately move towards cleaner fuel, perhaps electric.
And the policy decisions are taking place over a long period of time.
Amadmi party said we're going to bring buses, they brought it in the fag end of that year.
All these things have to happen faster.
One by one.
One by one.
One by one.
I'm asking the question.
I'm going to get responses and come back to you.

The transition to electro mobility has been tenfold from 2015 onwards, which includes because of incentives provided to the industry, which includes, you know, the entire charging infrastructure which is being created across the country.
But in our democracy, you know, these are
Can we do more for the national capital?
In a democracy, you have to leave the final choice of these things to the people of the country.

If I can shift to an electric vehicle... If you give more subsidies, once again, if you give more subsidies, you can attract the people towards that and that's also the role of the government, isn't it?
Subsidies are being provided.
In fact, I know at least 10 people in my friend circle who have opted for electrical vehicles.
I want to talk big picture.
If you look at any nation that has worked on air pollution and reversed it,
It has to be done through policy change that drives, that incentivizes good behavior and penalizes bad behavior.
People move towards EV mobility and I'm included in that because of the oil crisis.
The price of oil was going too high and I was like, you know, this is a better way.
I don't think the government influenced me too much.
because, you know, the battery price, the cars are more expensive.
But, you know, I went in that direction.

I would like to see more in terms of policy change to influence human behavior because the problem of air pollution and the problem of climate change will not go away unless we, you know, switch paths.
The path that we are on is not sustainable.
Raman, respond to that.
I think he has a very fair point.
Governments have an influence over human behavior and subsidies and such policies are going to be key in actually looking at whether we fight pollution or not.
An important point, Madhav, is that people also have a tendency to rebel.
Now, having said that, we are all witness to what happened into the government efforts on the reducing pollution by bringing in E20.
There was a political whole fiasco about it.
Barring that, the most important factor is so many buses came in, which were funded by the central scheme, but they were branded as if the outgoing Chief Minister is doing something great.
Then there is another important factor, Madhav, which we are not speaking about.

The kind of infrastructure that started as a policy matter from the days of Atal Bihari Vajpayee at the five end of his rule, his time, bringing in the concept of metro and the circular roads around Delhi and other things.
Those concepts were later carried on by the then Delhi government to some extent wherever they could.
And then, even going on today, if you see from your studios, if we have to go to Gurgaon, there's a new flyover which has come up.
And that has reduced the kind of traffic jams and everything that is happening.
Everybody knows what E20 is.
And E20 has gone to E35 also.
Ruining, destroying your vehicles, and it's functioning.
That's one part of it.
But here, I would talk about data manipulation versus accountability.
This government talks about 2047 and all.
Why can't they fix a five-year timeline that we can reduce by this time?
Because, see, we all worshiped during Diwali.
We celebrated Diwali.
We did not burn crackers.
Why?
Have we become less Hindus?
No.
Because our prayers say, sarve bhavan tu sukhi na, sarve santu niramaya, sarve bhadrani pasyantu, makasya dukhbha bhavet.
So if our religion talks about it,
Don't politicize it.
Simply fix up accountability.
Like we used to have five-year plans.
We used to give a result, report card after that.
But you can't go endlessly just talking about it, doing debates about it.
